classification.illumination_detail: internal white LEDs in each pan-channel element, fed by remote power supplies

knowledge.plain_language_summary: A storefront wall sign made of separate internally lit pan-channel elements: a logo 'cloud' (a shaped channel holding a pictorial mark in a filled disc), the brand wordmark as individual channel letters, and a small descriptor 'cloud' below. All elements are 5in deep with black returns and a 1in trim cap, lit with white LEDs behind 3/16in translucent white acrylic faces decorated with translucent and dual-color films. The wordmark mounts on a painted extruded raceway; the clouds flush-mount to the wall over remote power supplies.
knowledge.rationale: Building the mark as discrete pan-channel clouds plus individual channel letters gives a crisp dimensional daytime read and an even white-lit night read, while the raceway consolidates wiring and transformers for the wordmark and the remote supplies keep the clouds shallow against the wall.
knowledge.tradeoffs: Pan-channel letters with trim caps and translucent faces give a clean, serviceable, brightly lit storefront read, but cost more than flat-cut dimensional letters and require wall penetrations, a raceway, and remote power supplies.
knowledge.when_to_use: Tenant storefront identification where night illumination and a dimensional, branded read are required on a masonry or EIFS facade.

rules_observations: Single internal white LED source across all elements keeps night color consistent; dual-color film preserves the daytime two-tone read while unifying to white at night.
Clear hierarchy: logo cloud and wordmark dominate, descriptor cloud is subordinate in scale.
craft_observations: Trim-cap pan-channel construction with translucent faces is the conventional pro storefront build; black returns frame each lit face and hide the wall transition.
Raceway consolidates the wordmark wiring but adds a visible band; painting it to wall color is the standard move to suppress it.

aesthetic_notes.note: Dimensional clouds-plus-letters reads as a mid-market retail/service storefront identity rather than a minimal flush-cut treatment.
